install.command: python3 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install faster-whisper==1.2.1
install.size_note: venv on disk; models are extra and are downloaded on first use from huggingface.co: base.en ~145 MB, small.en ~480 MB (sizes from the Systran model cards, not measured here)
install.windows: yes (verified from PyPI release files 2026-10-29): ctranslate2 4.8.4 ships cp39..cp315 win_amd64 wheels; onnxruntime 1.31.1 ships cp311..cp314 win_amd64 + win_arm64; faster-whisper 1.2.1 is a pure-Python py3-none-any wheel; av 19.0.2 and numpy carry the 'Operating System :: Microsoft :: Windows' classifier. CPU only is enough (compute_type int8); no CUDA needed.

fixtures: fixtures/01-whisper: 3 synthetic English product-explainer narrations (keyboard.wav 38.9 s / 6 cues, thermos.wav 30.2 s / 5 cues, kettle.wav 30.3 s / 5 cues; espeak-ng en-us -s 150, per-sentence synthesis, silence-trimmed, 16 kHz mono s16, 0.4 s gaps so cue times are exact; 3.2 MB total). Per file: <name>.clean.srt (control, correct) and <name>.seeded.srt. KEY.json: 8 defects = 5 text (D1 45->54, D3 dropped 'smooth', D4 'Polar'->'Arctic' Flask, D6 added 'under', D7 temperature->pressure) + 3 timing (D2 start +450 ms, D5 cue -600 ms, D8 cue +900 ms). check_srt.py (faster-whisper word_timestamps -> difflib alignment of normalised tokens to cues -> per-cue WER, missing number/name tokens, start/end error ms), score.py (recall vs KEY, FPs on controls, runtime), make-fixtures.sh + gen_fixtures.py + make-fixtures.log (every command).

baseline.what: no ASR check (subtitles are timed from the script and the voice pipeline; nothing compares audio to cues)

logic_selftest.what: NOT an ASR measurement. score.py --mock feeds check_srt.py synthetic word timings derived from the clean SRTs (words spread evenly over each true cue) to verify the alignment, WER, number/name and timing logic end to end.
logic_selftest.note: With the first-draft threshold 0.05 < WER <= 0.08 the three single-word defects (1 word in 13-15 = WER 0.067-0.077) were missed, so the default threshold is 0.05. Real ASR errors on the TTS voice will therefore also land above the threshold; that is what the blocked run would have measured.

candidate_default.config: base.en, int8 on CPU, beam_size 1, word_timestamps=True, no VAD, WER threshold 0.05 per cue, timing limit 300 ms (end +200 ms slack), numbers normalised to digits, number/name tokens must be heard

limits: Model weights must come from huggingface.co on first run (or be copied into a folder and passed via --model-dir / WHISPER_MODEL_DIR); the sandbox denies that host, so no ASR ran here.

The checker is English-only as configured (base.en / small.en); the real task is 10 languages, which needs the multilingual 'base' / 'small' / 'medium' models (same API, --language xx), larger downloads and generally worse word timestamps for non-English.

Single-word defects force a per-cue WER threshold of 0.05 (one word in a <= 20-word cue); any ASR misrecognition of the TTS voice at that level is a false positive. The number/name rule is independent of the threshold and is the robust part.
Word end timestamps in Whisper are less precise than starts; the end check gets +200 ms slack. A start-only shift is still caught by the start check.

Fixture audio is espeak-ng (robotic). Real pipeline voices (neural TTS / human) usually transcribe better, so the sandbox numbers, once obtained, are a pessimistic bound for text and a fair test for timing.
CPU int8 runtime per 30-40 s clip was not measured; expect seconds for base.en and tens of seconds for small.en on a laptop CPU, plus a one-off model load.
verdict: NOT RUN (blocked: huggingface.co denied by network policy)
reason: Install, fixtures, checker, scorer and wrapper are complete and the detection logic passes an 8/8, 0-FP self-test on synthetic word timings, but the Whisper weights could not be fetched (proxy 403 to CONNECT huggingface.co:443), so recall/false positives/runtime of the real ASR are unmeasured. Owner can finish the trial locally with: bash runs/01-whisper/commands.sh (needs internet once, or a pre-downloaded model folder).
